Package dev.px.core.hud

Enum Class Anchor

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<Anchor>
dev.px.core.hud.Anchor
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<Anchor>, Constable
public enum Anchor extends Enum<Anchor>
The screen reference point an element is positioned relative to.

This enum is where most of the HUD system's behaviour actually lives. Storing position as an anchor plus an offset, rather than as absolute screen coordinates, buys three things for free:

  • Resolution independence. A bottom-right element stays in the bottom-right corner when the window is resized, instead of being flung off-screen or stranded in the middle.
  • Correct growth direction. The - a * size term means a right-anchored element grows leftwards, a bottom-anchored one grows upwards, and a centred one grows both ways. This falls out of the formula, so no code anywhere special-cases growth.
  • Stable edge gaps. An offset means "distance from my anchor", which is what a user setting up a HUD actually intends.

The factors are always 0, 0.5 or 1, for the near edge, the centre, and the far edge of the axis.

      public float offsetXFor(float screenWidth, float x, float width)
      The inverse of resolveX(float, float, float): the offset that would place an element of width at absolute x.

      Needed whenever something works in absolute coordinates and has to be written back as layout state, which is every drag and every anchor change.

    • nearest

      public static Anchor nearest(float centerX, float centerY, float screenWidth, float screenHeight)
      Returns:
      the anchor whose reference point is closest to the given position, as a fraction of the screen. Lets an editor re-anchor an element to the corner it was dropped nearest, so it behaves sensibly on the next resolution change.
